name: Kunza
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Schuller, R. R. 1908. Vocabularios y nuevos materiales.. lengua de los indios Lican-Antai (Atacamenos) (123pp sketch); San Roman 1890 — not online; Vaisse et al. 1896 Glosario (archive.org) checked, no stress statement

sources.citation: San Román, Francisco J. 1890. La lengua cunza de los naturales de Atacama. Santiago: Imprenta Gutenberg (Revista de la Dirección de Obras Públicas, Sección de Minas y Geografía), 20 pp.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Tozzer Library, call number SPEC.COLL. S.A. Sa 51.8 c)
sources.harvard_location: Tozzer Library, call number SPEC.COLL. S.A. Sa 51.8 c
sources.note: Only orthographic/pronunciation notes (pp. 19-20): strong aspirations with vowel prolongation written with an 'acento circunflejo', geminate consonants pronounced separately (cap-pin, ac-ca), c vs k. Nothing on where stress falls.

sources.citation: Fabre, Alain. 2005- (entry rev. 2009). Kunza. In: Diccionario etnolingüístico y guía bibliográfica de los pueblos indígenas sudamericanos.
sources.note: Bibliographic guide; states 'Sobre la estructura de la lengua kunza, no se ha publicado nada'. Lists Mostny 1954 'Apuntes sobre el cunza', Lehnert 1976, 1987, Echeverría y Reyes 1890, Tschudi 1971 [1869]/Sáez 1971, Siarez 2003.

sources.citation: Peyró García, Miguel. 2006b. Relación de estudios y documentos sobre la antigua lengua de Atacama (web bibliography, geocities, archived 2009).
sources.note: Bibliography only; confirms Adelaar & Muysken 2004 'The Atacameño language' pp. 375-384, Lehnert Santander 1976 (Cuadernos de Filología 5: 71-80), Lehnert 1987, Mostny et al. 1954, Siarez 2003/2004, Tschudi 1869 vol. V p. 77.

sources.citation: Schuller, Rodolfo R. 1908 [1907]. Vocabularios y nuevos materiales para el estudio de la lengua de los indios Lican-Antai (Atacameños)-Calchaquí. Santiago: F. Becerra (Biblioteca de Lingüística Americana 2), 123 pp.
sources.note: Comparative vocabularies and name lists; p. 25 'Muy poco de positivo se sabe del sistema fonético del idioma atacameño' followed by Lenz's remarks on glottalized stops. No accent/stress statement anywhere (a full-text search for stress/accent acent/tónic/sílaba negative; introduction and grammatical sections read).

sources.citation: Schuller, R. R. (1908). Vocabularios y nuevos materiales para el estudio de la lengua de los indios Lican-Antai (Atacameños) Calchaqui. Santiago: F. Becerra M. 123 pp.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library, call number 1272.63.11; Tozzer Library (offsite storage), call number AM.LING. B 472 (2))
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library, call number 1272.63.11; Tozzer Library (offsite storage), call number AM.LING. B 472 (2)
sources.note: Language not in the catalog; no existing statements. The HathiTrust open_url is confirmed full view by the catalog API (rightsCode pdus, 'Full view') but the babel page and the imgsrv plaintext endpoint both could not be reached by automated download 'Blocked from HathiTrust' bot challenges by automated download, so the work was read from the identical archive.org/Memoria Chilena scan already saved held by the project (same title page: Biblioteca de Lingüística Americana tomo II, F. Becerra, Santiago; 123 pp.).

sources.citation: Peyró García, Miguel. 2005. Estructuras gramaticales en el Glosario de la lengua atacameña (1896). LIAMES 5: 25-42. doi:10.20396/liames.v5i1.1437
sources.note: 'Notas sobre la estructura fonológica' (pp. 29-31) treats segments only (vowels a e i o u; consonants ʔ p k t c s m n ñ l r). The only mention of accent (p. 37) is a speculation that pronoun i-a vs determiner -ja 'deben haberse marcado en la lengua mediante la presencia o no de un acento de palabra propio' — no statement of stress placement.

sources.citation: Adelaar, Willem F. H. with Pieter C. Muysken. 2004. The Languages of the Andes. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 'The Atacameño language' pp. 375-384 (phonology pp. 376-380).
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Dumbarton Oaks Library, call number PM5100.A34 2004X; Tozzer Library, call number S.A. Ad 32 l)
sources.harvard_location: Dumbarton Oaks Library, call number PM5100 .A34 2004X; Tozzer Library, call number S.A. Ad 32 l
sources.note: The only modern synthesis of Kunza phonology (source for WALS, PHOIBLE/SAPHON, Wikipedia); if any modern statement on Kunza stress exists it is here. Google Books search-inside returned 0 pages for 'Kunza stress' before blocking; 'Atacameño stress' untested.

sources.citation: Vilte Vilte, Julio. 2004. Kunza: diccionario kunza-español / español-kunza: lengua del pueblo lickan antai o atacameño. [Chile]: CODELCO, 88 pp.
sources.note: Prose section 'El kunza y sus características' (pp. 12-13) says only that gestures 'complementaba la acentuación' of the language and that it sounded harsh; dictionary entries carry no stress marks; no rule.

sources.citation: WALS Online, Atacameño (wals_code_atm), source Adelaar 2004; PHOIBLE inventory 2123 (SAPHON) for Kunza, source Adelaar & Muysken 2004; Grambank kunz1244 (sources Peyró García 2005, San Román 1890, Torero 2002).
sources.note: WALS has no values for Atacameño in stress features 14A-17A (valueset pages 404); PHOIBLE/Grambank code no stress information.

sources.citation: Buchwald, Otto von. 1923 [1922]. Análisis de una gramática atacameña. Boletín de la Academia Nacional de Historia (Quito) 5: 292-301; offprint Quito: Tip. Salesianas, 10 pp.
sources.note: 'El alfabeto' section re-states San Román's letters (geminates, h as spiritus asper); rest is morphology and Quechua/Aymara comparisons. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Vaïsse, Emilio F; Hoyos, Félix 2º; Echeverría y Reyes, Aníbal. 1896. Glosario de la lengua atacameña. Santiago: Imprenta Cervantes (Anales de la Universidad de Chile 91), with 'Informe' by Rodolfo Lenz.
sources.note: Letter-value notes only (ck, h, pp, tt, tch, y); Lenz's report discusses glottalized stops. No statement on stress (also checked via the wikisource transcription).

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Kunza language' (en) and 'Kunza' (es); Glottolog 5.x record kunz1244.
sources.note: Phonology sections (segments, possible vowel length) with no stress statement; used for their reference lists (Mostny 1954, Lehnert 1987, Moore 1878, Vilte 2004, Adelaar 2004 pp. 376/380).

sources.citation: Mostny, Grete. 1954. Apuntes sobre el Kunza. In Mostny, G., F. Jeldes, R. González & F. Oberhauser, Peine, un pueblo atacameño, pp. 139-170. Santiago: Universidad de Chile, Instituto de Geografía (Publicación 4).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Last field notes taken from people who still remembered Kunza forms and songs; a 30-page linguistic appendix likely to include pronunciation remarks, possibly accent.

sources.citation: Gundermann K., Hans. 2014. Guía para Educadores Tradicionales Cultura Licanantai y Lengua Kunsa: Programa de Educación Intercultural Bilingüe. Santiago: Gobierno de Chile, Ministerio de Educación.
